title: Twenty First Word First Station Fifth Warning Two Spiritual Mines And The Loss Of Abandoning Prayer

questions.question: What is the first spiritual benefit mentioned for someone who works in a garden with a proper intention?
questions.answer: That person receives a share in the worshipful praise made by the plants and trees he cultivates.

questions.question: According to the passage, what condition is attached to gaining that first benefit?
questions.answer: The work must be done with a sound and sincere intention.

questions.question: What is the second benefit connected to the garden’s produce?
questions.answer: Whatever is consumed from it can count like charity on the worker’s behalf.

questions.question: Who can eat from the produce and still make that second benefit apply?
questions.answer: Any creature or person mentioned there, including animals, people, customers, and even thieves.

questions.question: What two attitudes must a person have for the produce to count like charity?
questions.answer: He must work for Allah’s sake and stay within what Allah allows, while seeing himself as a caretaker distributing Allah’s property.

questions.question: Why does leaving the required prayers lead to a major loss in this passage?
questions.answer: Because the person misses both spiritual gains, loses motivation, and is deprived of a deeper meaning in his work.

questions.question: How is the prayerless person described over time as he gets older?
questions.answer: He becomes tired of his work, loses heart, and drifts into laziness.

questions.question: What kind of thinking pushes that person toward idleness?
questions.answer: He thinks he will soon leave the world anyway, so he sees no reason to keep struggling.

questions.question: How does the other person think differently about work and worship?
questions.answer: He sees both lawful work and worship as ways to prepare for the grave and the next life, so he works with more energy.

questions.question: What contrast does the passage draw between the two workers?
questions.answer: One becomes spiritually bankrupt and discouraged, while the other becomes more purposeful, hopeful, and hardworking.

questions.question: In the passage, what does the image of the “first mine” represent?
questions.answer: It represents a hidden spiritual gain a person receives through sincere work in the garden.

questions.question: How does the passage connect farming or gardening with worship?
questions.answer: It teaches that ordinary work can bring spiritual reward when it is done with the right intention and in obedience to Allah.

questions.question: What does the “second mine” add beyond the first one?
questions.answer: It adds the reward of ongoing charity when others benefit from what the garden produces.

questions.question: Does the second reward depend only on the produce itself, or also on the worker’s outlook and method?
questions.answer: It also depends on the worker’s outlook and method, especially acting within Allah’s permission and for His sake.

questions.question: Why is the worker told to see himself as a distributor rather than an owner in an absolute sense?
questions.answer: Because the passage teaches that the true ownership belongs to Allah, and the worker is only delivering what Allah provides.

questions.question: What happens to the person who abandons the prescribed prayers, according to the passage?
questions.answer: He loses these two great gains and ends up with weakened spirit and poor motivation.

questions.question: In what sense does the passage call that person “bankrupt”?
questions.answer: He is spiritually emptied of the rewards and meanings that could have enriched his life and work.

questions.question: What emotional change happens in the neglectful person as old age comes?
questions.answer: His interest fades, and he becomes worn out and detached from his work.

questions.question: What future-oriented goal gives the first man strength?
questions.answer: He wants to prepare light for the grave and provision for the life to come.

questions.question: What major lesson about prayer and daily work comes out of the whole passage?
questions.answer: Prayer does not take away from meaningful work; instead, it gives work spiritual value, purpose, and lasting reward.

questions.question: What practical setting is used in the passage to explain the lesson?
questions.answer: The lesson is explained through the example of working in a garden.

questions.question: What is gained from flowers and fruit-bearing trees when the intention is right?
questions.answer: A share in the glorification and praise connected with those living things.

questions.question: Why is intention so central in the first part of the passage?
questions.answer: Because the outward action alone is not enough; the inner purpose turns the work into something spiritually rewarding.

questions.question: What kinds of eaters are included in the discussion of the garden’s produce?
questions.answer: Both expected and unexpected users are included, from people and animals to even those who take it wrongly.

questions.question: What limits must be respected for the produce to count as charity?
questions.answer: The worker must act in Allah’s name and remain inside the lawful boundaries set by Him.

questions.question: What losses come from quitting the required prayers in this example?
questions.answer: The person loses major unseen rewards, his morale weakens, and his work becomes empty of higher purpose.

questions.question: How does the passage portray the long-term effect of a purely worldly mindset on work?
questions.answer: It makes a person eventually resent the work and lose the will to continue.

questions.question: What does the committed person hope to increase through harder effort?
questions.answer: He hopes to increase both his worship and his lawful work so that his reward in the next life grows.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the relationship between this life and the next?
questions.answer: Actions in this life can become investments for the next life when they are guided by prayer, sincerity, and lawful conduct.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the value of sincere intention in ordinary labor?
questions.answer: It teaches that sincere intention can turn ordinary labor into a source of worship and reward.

questions.question: How are the plants and trees connected to the worker’s reward?
questions.answer: Their acts of glorifying Allah become a source of reward for the worker who raises them with the right intention.

questions.question: What transforms the eating of garden produce into something like charity?
questions.answer: Working for Allah’s sake and treating the produce as something entrusted by Him.

questions.question: Why does the passage even mention thieves among those who may eat from the produce?
questions.answer: To show how broad the reward can be when the worker’s intention and conduct are sound.

questions.question: What view of property is taught in the phrase about being a distribution official?
questions.answer: It teaches stewardship, meaning the person handles provision as a trustee, not as an independent owner.

questions.question: Why does giving up prayer damage a person’s morale according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because prayer helps connect daily effort to lasting reward, and without that connection the person loses heart.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the spiritual and motivational condition of the one who stops praying?
questions.answer: He becomes deprived, discouraged, and inwardly emptied.

questions.question: What statement shows the older neglectful worker has fallen into a narrow view of life?
questions.answer: He thinks there is no point in effort since he will leave the world anyway.

questions.question: What mindset keeps the other worker active instead of passive?
questions.answer: He believes his work and worship are building benefit for the grave and the hereafter.

questions.question: If you had to sum up the warning of this passage in one sentence, what would it be?
questions.answer: Do not let prayer slip away, because it gives your lawful work meaning, reward, and strength that you would otherwise lose.

questions.question: What hidden reward is connected to caring for a garden with good intention?
questions.answer: The caretaker shares in the devotional praise connected with the plants and trees.

questions.question: Is that reward tied mainly to the size of the garden or to the state of the heart?
questions.answer: It is tied to the state of the heart, especially sincere intention.

questions.question: What hidden reward is connected to the produce after it leaves the garden?
questions.answer: Its consumption can be recorded like charity for the worker.

questions.question: What three main conditions shape that second reward in the passage?
questions.answer: Working for Allah, staying within what is lawful, and viewing oneself as a servant distributing Allah’s provision.

questions.question: How does the passage reframe farm work or garden work?
questions.answer: It presents it as more than earning a living; it can also become a path to spiritual gain.

questions.question: What does the person lose by neglecting the required prayers while doing such work?
questions.answer: He loses the two great benefits that would have enriched and encouraged him.

questions.question: What inner result follows that loss?
questions.answer: His determination weakens and his spirit drops.

questions.question: What outward result appears later in his behavior?
questions.answer: He becomes lazy and no longer wants to keep working.

questions.question: What belief strengthens the other person’s willingness to work harder?
questions.answer: He believes his effort can benefit him after death by preparing reward and light for the next life.

questions.question: What comparison between the two people is most important in this passage?
questions.answer: One sees work as temporary and empty, while the other sees it as a means of worship and eternal benefit.

questions.question: What are the “two mines” in the passage?
questions.answer: They are two valuable spiritual gains hidden within lawful garden work: sharing in the praise of the plants and receiving charity-like reward from what others consume.

questions.question: Why is the first one called a “mine”?
questions.answer: Because it is a precious benefit that is not obvious at first but can be discovered through sincere understanding.

questions.question: Why is the second one also described as a valuable hidden gain?
questions.answer: Because even the produce eaten by many kinds of creatures can become reward for the worker under the right conditions.

questions.question: What role does lawful action play in receiving these benefits?
questions.answer: It is essential, since the work must remain within Allah’s permitted boundaries.

questions.question: How does the passage define the worker’s proper self-understanding?
questions.answer: He should see himself as entrusted with delivering Allah’s provision, not as the final owner in an independent sense.

questions.question: What strong phrase is used for the one who leaves prayer, and what does it mean?
questions.answer: He is described as bankrupt, meaning he has thrown away major spiritual capital.

questions.question: How does losing prayer eventually affect the person’s relationship to his job?
questions.answer: It drains his enthusiasm until he no longer sees value in continuing.

questions.question: What kind of speech reflects the discouraged worker’s attitude?
questions.answer: He speaks as if worldly departure makes present effort pointless.

questions.question: How does the praying worker connect present effort with life after death?
questions.answer: He believes more worship and lawful work will send benefit ahead for the grave and the hereafter.

questions.question: What broader principle about Islam and daily labor is taught by the whole passage?
questions.answer: When a Muslim joins sincere intention, lawful conduct, and prayer, daily labor becomes both worldly effort and worship.
